Bennett holds a B.S. in information systems with training in configuration management, Unix administration and formal change control, and came from release coordination at a financial data-processing organization with strict uptime requirements.

Bennett was reliable and diplomatic but persistent when a team went around change control, while accepting that urgency sometimes requires an exception. Releases followed numbered checklists, each change carried its approval reference, and deployment records were compared with the version actually installed.

Bennett signed nine register revisions: the tiered SAN (February 2007), the 10 Gb core racks (March 2007), the virtualization hosts, RCK-05 B (May 2007), the staged SAN firmware upgrade, RCK-02 F and G (September and December 2009), and the GPU nodes, RCK-04 E (March 2010), and drew the inventories INV-001 E and F. Bennett also checked the OER-3 proximity card drawing. Bennett left OER on 31 May 2010.
bios.OER-2007-001:
Pamela Crawley held the Red Crew day COMM seat from May 2007 to the end of September 2010. Crawley grew up in Oakland, California, and served four years as an Army signal specialist before coming to OER.

Lorraine Varga trained Crawley on the floor. Crawley organized a shift well and had the dry humor to carry a long one. Crawley was at the COMM desk on 13 August 2007, the morning severe weather warnings began arriving by internet alert feed, with the satellite receiver kept as backup; from then on a missing warning was reported to Communications, which meant to Crawley. Crawley also worked the May 2009 flu precautions, when headsets became personal and hand sanitizer appeared at every console.

Crawley came to the Red day COMM desk after Tamara Ortiz and Sandra Lacey had each held it for a year or so, and stayed three and a half years, long enough to give the seat some continuity again. Crawley's call log from those years is tidy and short, and the Red day crew of the time remembers Crawley as the person who could make a long, quiet shift go faster.

Off shift Crawley was a licensed amateur radio operator and painted. Crawley left OER on 30 September 2010.
bios.OER-2007-002:
Sonia Patel was database and archive administrator from May 2007 to September 2015, following Martin Feldman. Patel holds a BS in computer science with training in database recovery and information lifecycle management, and came from managing long-lived operational records, retention schedules and recovery procedures across older and newer storage.

Patel was patient and exacting and did not trust a successful job status until the records underneath it had been checked. Restore tests were recorded, record counts were compared before and after every migration, and media age and format dependencies were tracked year by year.

Patel drew compression on the node links, SWA-002 D (February 2008), and GPU correlation with virtualized support services, SWA-001 G (June 2010), and carried the archive through the SAN upgrades of 2009 and the flash tier for the live database in 2013. Patel left in September 2015 for a senior records infrastructure role, and Calvin Brooks took over in 2016.
bios.OER-2007-003:
Jared Lennox was the Red Crew floater from August 2007 to the end of May 2008. Lennox grew up in Flint, Michigan, and served as a Navy electronics technician before joining OER.

Walter Dunmore trained Lennox, and some of Dunmore's formality rubbed off: Lennox was courteous, careful with ambiguous data and good at catching small timing drifts. As floater Lennox covered all four Red seats, day and night, in the months after the floor moved to proximity badges and the internet severe-weather alert feed went into service.

A floater on the Red crew works whichever seat is empty, and in 2007 that often meant nights under Dunmore, who still called everyone by surname and expected the log to be complete before the handoff. Lennox fitted that routine well and left handoff notes that the next person could pick up without a question.

Away from work Lennox took photographs and played chess. Lennox left OER on 31 May 2008.
bios.OER-2007-004:
Shane Baptiste held the Blue Crew day COMM seat from September 2007 to the end of March 2009. Baptiste came to OER from an alarm-monitoring station, where every call was a stranger's bad night and the job was to stay calm and write it down.

Craig Lowry, newly the Blue Day Lead, trained Baptiste on the seat Lowry had held for seven years. Baptiste was calm on the phone and alert to timing drifts. On 31 December 2008 Baptiste was on duty when a leap second was inserted at 17:59:60 local, and helped check that the wall clocks, time servers and log stamps all agreed.

Blue Day COMM was the seat Lowry knew best, and Baptiste had the advantage of a Lead who could answer any question about it from memory. Baptiste's eighteen months covered the first full year of the internet severe-weather alerts and the long run of hurricane season 2008, when Hurricane Ike took Node 4 (Gulf / Texas) off the board for most of two days.

Off shift Baptiste went camping and fixed old cars. Baptiste left OER on 31 March 2009.
bios.OER-2008-001:
Nicole Mathis held the Red Crew day Correlation seat from February 2008 to the end of February 2012. Mathis studied computer science at Drake University and analyzed data for a transportation agency before OER.

Lorraine Varga trained Mathis. Mathis read everything twice and could take the heat out of a tense call, a useful pair of habits at a correlation desk. Mathis worked the May 2009 flu precautions and was on the floor on 8 November 2010, the first morning of the video wall, when display faults went straight to Engineering and everyone learned where the tiles had moved.

Mathis took the Red day correlation desk after Jeffrey Underhill and held it for four years under two Leads, Joanne Tillman and then Lorraine Varga. Mathis's correlation notes from those years are known for saying, in one line, which reports were matched and why.

Mathis sang in a choir and liked cooking for a crowd. Mathis left OER on 29 February 2012.
bios.OER-2008-002:
Marvin Poole spent eleven years on the Blue Crew: floater from April 2008, night Monitoring from November 2009 and Blue Night Lead from November 2018 to the end of September 2019. Poole studied environmental science at Arizona State University and worked at an alarm-monitoring station before OER.

Craig Lowry trained Poole, and Poole became one of the busiest trainers the night crew has had: Wayne Gutierrez, Caden Pacheco, Beverly Ashby and Courtney Marlow all learned the floor from Poole. Poole was on the Monitoring desk in the early hours of 11 March 2011, when the Pacific tsunami bulletin came in and the night crew watched the coastal reports.

Poole's nine years on the Blue night Monitoring desk spanned the change from the old displays to the video wall in November 2010 and the arrival of the real power grid tile in 2015. When Lamar Iverson left in 2018, Poole took the Lead seat for the last year, handing it to Beverly Ashby, whom Poole had trained.

Poole was a good listener and kept precise logs. Gail Everett was a friend from the early night years. Off shift: woodworking and board games. Poole left OER on 30 September 2019.
bios.OER-2008-003:
Reuben Schaefer spent twelve years on the Red day watch: floater from August 2008, then COMM from January 2011 to the end of October 2020. Schaefer studied engineering technology at Gannon University and worked as a trucking dispatcher before coming to OER.

Walter Dunmore trained Schaefer, who was hard to rattle, picked up new tools quickly and wrote clear handoffs. Schaefer was on the COMM desk on 6 July 2015, the first day the power grid tile showed regional electricity demand from published national data, for the leap second of 31 December 2016, and on 16 March 2020, the first morning of pandemic precautions, with every other console in use and handover by phone bridge. Schaefer trained Camila Satterfield and Selena Crowe.

Off shift Schaefer quilted and fished. Schaefer left OER on 31 October 2020.
bios.OER-2008-004:
Irene Donahue sat Blue Crew day Monitoring from October 2008 to the end of May 2009. Donahue studied information systems at the University of Oregon and worked on a cable company's network before OER.

Craig Lowry trained Donahue, who was good at odd faults and quick with new tools. Donahue arrived in time for the leap second of 31 December 2008 and helped the day crew check the clocks and log stamps that evening, and worked the start of the May 2009 flu precautions.

Donahue came to the Blue day crew in the months after Keith Espinoza left the Monitoring desk, and took over a board that had been watched by Imani Rhodes for eight years before that. Donahue's short time on the floor was spent mostly learning which of the old tiles could be trusted, a lesson the floor passed on to every new hire.

Away from the floor Donahue played chess and rode a bicycle. Donahue left OER on 31 May 2009.
bios.OER-2008-005:
Patricia "Pat" O'Neill was security and system integrity engineer from November 2008 to July 2010. O'Neill holds a B.S. in computer information systems with training in configuration auditing and change management, and came from enterprise change control, reconciling approved maintenance requests with what was actually configured on the hosts.

O'Neill was patient but firm. An approved change was not assumed to have been done correctly, and an undocumented one was not assumed to be malicious; either way the difference had to be explained and recorded. O'Neill wrote every finding in three parts, labeled expected, observed and disposition, and followed an open discrepancy from one review cycle to the next until it was closed with a verification.

O'Neill's time covered the SAN firmware upgrades of 2009 and the GPU nodes of 2010. O'Neill left OER on 31 July 2010, and Kevin Wallace took over in November.
bios.OER-2008-006:
Michelle Carter looked after OER's servers and infrastructure from December 2008 to July 2014, following James Holloway. Carter holds a BS in computer engineering with training in Unix administration and virtualization, and came from a regional enterprise computing environment, including some of its early virtualization projects.

Carter was calm and pragmatic, favored controlled migrations over rushed modernization, and expected every maintenance job to come with a recovery plan. Host inventories were kept current, checks were recorded before and after each change, and capacity trends and recurring hardware faults were tracked. Disciplined virtualization and capacity planning arrived with Carter.

Carter drew 17 register revisions: the staged SAN firmware (2009), the GPU nodes (March 2010), overhead cable trays, FLR-001 G (March 2010), the thin-bezel video wall, FLR-002 E (November 2010), the distributed batch cluster (2011), IPv6 and the cellular backup path that replaced the dial-back modems (August 2011), the UPS replacement (2012), the leaf-spine cabinets (May 2013) and the flash tier for the live database, RCK-02 H (July 2013). Carter left in July 2014 for a senior infrastructure post.
bios.OER-2009-001:
Dominic Landry sat Red Crew day Monitoring from January 2009 to the end of November 2013, taking the desk when Lorraine Varga moved up to Lead. Landry came to OER from an alarm-monitoring station.

Varga trained Landry on the desk Varga had just left. Landry organized a shift well and was a good listener. Landry was on the board for the May 2009 flu precautions and on 8 November 2010, the first morning of the video wall, and worked through the change to OER-4 smart cards in March 2012 and the Sandy year that followed.

Landry's five years at the Red day Monitoring desk covered the change from the old displays to the video wall and the first years of the cellular backup path to the regional sites. Landry was known for a calm handoff and for noticing when a tile had been quiet for too long.

Angela Vail on the Red night crew was a friend. Off shift Landry played softball and rode a bicycle. Landry left OER on 30 November 2013.
bios.OER-2009-002:
Marcellus Granger sat Blue Crew day Monitoring from July 2009 to the end of June 2014. Granger grew up in Syracuse, New York, and served as a Navy electronics technician before joining OER.

Craig Lowry trained Granger, who read everything twice and wrote precise logs and handoffs. Granger was on the board on 29 August 2011, when Engineering removed the dial-back modems and the dial-up tile began to read NO CARRIER by design; on 5 March 2012, the first morning of OER-4 smart cards; and on 9 April 2014, when every account was reset after a widely published security flaw.

Granger came to the Blue day crew after Irene Donahue's short time at the Monitoring desk and gave it five steady years. Granger also worked the first morning of the video wall in November 2010, when the tiles moved and display faults went straight to Engineering.

Leonard Fitch was a friend and a frequent shift-swap partner. Off shift: quilting and fishing. Granger left OER on 30 June 2014.
bios.OER-2009-003:
Nathan Navarro held the Blue Crew day COMM seat from October 2009 to the end of July 2014. Navarro studied at North Dakota State University and worked at an alarm-monitoring station before OER.

Russell Saldana trained Navarro, who cross-checked records carefully and was patient with new staff. Navarro was on the COMM desk for the removal of the dial-back modems on 29 August 2011, the first morning of OER-4 smart cards on 5 March 2012, when forgotten PINs went to Security and not to colleagues, and the password reset of 9 April 2014.

Blue Day COMM had been Lowry's seat for seven years and then Baptiste's; Navarro made it a long tenure again, nearly five years, and was the voice most regional contacts heard from the Blue day crew in that time. Navarro's call log was always in time order and always complete.

Off shift Navarro ran and baked. Navarro left OER on 31 July 2014.
bios.OER-2009-004:
Glenn Rowan was the Blue Crew floater from December 2009 to the end of August 2011. Rowan studied computer science and worked in cloud operations before coming to OER, one of the first watch hires from that kind of background.

Lamar Iverson trained Rowan. Rowan wrote clear handoffs and stayed steady under pressure, with a dry wit. As floater Rowan covered the Blue seats through the arrival of the video wall in November 2010 and the Pacific tsunami bulletin of March 2011.

Rowan brought a newer kind of experience to the floor at a time when more of the regional data was arriving over the internet, and was often the person the crew asked when a feed came in late or in an odd format. Rowan learned every Blue seat in under two years and was trusted on any of them.

Away from work Rowan rode a bicycle and fixed old cars. Rowan left OER on 31 August 2011.
bios.OER-2010-001:
Evan Brooks was communications and external feeds engineer from February 2010 to August 2016. Brooks holds a BS in computer engineering with vendor training in network appliances and integration, and came from a managed infrastructure provider, supporting gateway replacements, remote monitoring connections and customer data interfaces.

Brooks disliked repetitive manual recovery and was comfortable changing an established configuration when testing supported it. Reusable diagnostic scripts replaced many of the old step-by-step recoveries, configuration snapshots were taken before and after each change, and a feed was always tested from the receiving end rather than from a green link light.

Brooks's years saw more of OER's outside data move to internet delivery. In July 2015 the power grid tile began showing regional electricity demand from published hourly national data, and the next year the collectors and feed handlers moved into containers. Brooks left in August 2016 for a broader infrastructure role, and Lila Morgan took over in 2017.
bios.OER-2010-002:
Alan Pierce was data quality and correlation engineer from April 2010 to September 2014, following Claire Donnelly. Pierce holds a BS in computer science with database administration and statistical-process training, and came from data integrity work for a telecommunications operations group, investigating conflicting event records between network-management and billing systems.

Pierce was quietly persistent and preferred a repeatable test to a judgment call. Small test datasets were built for every disputed case, false matches and missed correlations were counted, and each change to a rule was recorded together with its measured effect.

Pierce arrived just before correlation moved to GPU nodes in June 2010, and spent much of the next four years measuring how the faster system behaved, including the forty minutes after the June 2012 leap second when correlation ran slow until the servers were restarted. Pierce left in September 2014 for a senior role in a larger data-integration program.
bios.OER-2010-003:
Ronald Lavoie led the Red Crew night watch from July 2010 to the end of January 2011, the first Lead after Walter Dunmore's twelve years in the seat. Lavoie grew up in Newark, New Jersey, and served four years as an Air Force communications specialist.

Lavoie inherited Dunmore's checklist from the top drawer, along with the note left for the successor, and kept the night crew on its routine through the change. Lavoie read ambiguous data carefully and wrote precise log entries, and led the Red nights through the first months of the video wall.

Lavoie's short time as Lead came at a turning point for the Red night crew: Dunmore had just retired after twelve years, Garrity and Voigt had been on the crew since 1998, and Angela Vail had been on Monitoring since 2003. Lavoie kept the routine the crew already knew and changed very little, which suited them.

Off shift Lavoie did woodworking and photography. Lavoie left OER on 31 January 2011.
bios.OER-2010-004:
Michael Turner ran configuration and release from September 2010 to December 2014, following Laura Bennett. Turner holds an associate degree in computer systems technology with training in Unix administration, version control and release management, and came from systems operations, supporting scheduled deployments and maintenance windows for a multi-site enterprise.

Turner moved into configuration work after noticing, repeatedly, that the approved release records did not match the installed software. A handwritten deployment checklist sat next to the electronic records, version strings were compared before and after each change, and a failed step was recorded instead of quietly repeated. Turner would stop a release when the installed baseline could not be verified.

Turner signed seven register revisions: checking the distributed batch cluster, RCK-05 C (March 2011), the OER-4 smart cards, SEC-001 F (March 2012), the spine switches (May 2013) and the flash tier for the live database (July 2013), and drawing the inventories INV-001 G and INV-002 D. Turner left OER on 31 December 2014.
bios.OER-2010-005:
Kevin Wallace was security and system integrity engineer from November 2010 to April 2013, following Pat O'Neill. Wallace holds an associate degree in network administration with vendor training in Unix security, account auditing and incident response, and came from administering mixed Unix and legacy servers.

Wallace moved into security after finding, more than once, that stale accounts and undocumented local changes undermined the formal access policy. Wallace accepted that old systems cannot always meet modern standards, but expected every exception to have an owner and a reason. Last-login records and effective permissions were checked, and a list of orphaned accounts was kept until each one had an owner or was closed.

Wallace drew SEC-001 F, the OER-4 smart cards with PIN that went into use on 5 March 2012, when card and PIN both became necessary at the watch floor door. Wallace left OER on 30 April 2013.
bios.OER-2010-006:
Michael Grant served as systems architect and technical lead from November 2010 to June 2017, succeeding Catherine Doyle. Grant holds an MS in computer science and a BS in computer engineering, and came from principal systems engineering on a distributed enterprise platform, coordinating architecture across infrastructure, data services and separately maintained applications.

Grant was calm and persuasive and preferred changes that could prove their benefit one step at a time; designs that assumed every part could be upgraded together were treated with care. Dependency diagrams and decision records were kept current, each team was asked to write down its rollback path, and open exceptions were reviewed at every major change.

Grant approved 26 register revisions: the thin-bezel video wall (November 2010), the fuel polishing system (2011), IPv6 and the cellular backup path (August 2011), the UPS replacement (2012), the 40 Gb leaf-spine fabric, NET-006 A (May 2013), the flash tier (July 2013), 10 Gb wavelengths to every node, NET-002 J (April 2014), object storage for the archive (2016) and hot aisle containment, FLR-001 J (September 2016). Grant left in June 2017 for a principal architecture role.
bios.OER-2011-001:
Theresa Valdez spent more than six years on the Red day watch: floater from February 2011, then Correlation from April 2012 to the end of August 2017. Valdez studied computer science at the University of Michigan-Dearborn and worked in cloud operations before OER.

Valdez remembered past incidents in detail and could calm a tense call. Valdez was on the correlation desk on 6 July 2015, the first day of the real power grid tile, and for the leap second of 31 December 2016, and worked the floor through Sandy in 2012 and the internet name-service outage of October 2016.

Valdez spent the first year as the Red floater, learning all four seats in the months after the Pacific tsunami bulletin, and then held the day correlation desk for more than five years under Lorraine Varga. Valdez was the person the crew asked when a pattern looked familiar, because Valdez usually remembered when it had happened before.

Off shift Valdez went camping and sang in a choir. Valdez left OER on 31 August 2017.
bios.OER-2011-002:
Quincy Paxton held the Blue Crew night Correlation seat from June 2011 to the end of November 2012. Paxton studied psychology at the University of South Alabama before coming to OER.

Lamar Iverson trained Paxton, who was formal, courteous and careful with ambiguous data. Paxton joined the night crew in the months after the Pacific tsunami bulletin and worked through the removal of the dial-back modems, the leap second of June 2012 and Sandy in October 2012, when Nodes 1 and 2 ran on generator.

Night correlation on the Blue crew had been Gail Everett's desk for seven years, and Paxton took it on soon after Everett left. Paxton's notes from those months are formal and exact, and include the hourly node power checks of the Sandy night.

Away from work Paxton played board games and fished. Paxton left OER on 30 November 2012.
bios.OER-2011-003:
Valerie Tate led the Red Crew night watch from August 2011 to the end of March 2018. Tate came to OER from supervising data entry for an insurance carrier.

Terrence Garrity trained Tate, and Tate went on to train Bruce Norwood, Travis Bryce and Lyle Jarrett. Tate was the Lead on 30 June 2012, when correlation ran slow for about forty minutes after the leap second until Engineering restarted the servers; on 29 October 2012, when Sandy put Nodes 1 and 2 on generator and the crew rechecked node power every hour; and for the leap second of 30 June 2015.

Tate took the Red night Lead seat after Ronald Lavoie and held it for nearly seven years, longer than anyone since Dunmore. Tate's crew included Terrence Garrity until Garrity's last night in July 2012 and Renata Voigt throughout, and Tate learned a great deal from both.

Tate stayed steady under pressure and learned new tools quickly. Off shift: cycling and running. Tate left OER on 31 March 2018.
bios.OER-2011-004:
Jessica Merritt was the Blue Crew floater from December 2011 to the end of March 2013. Merritt studied communication at West Texas A&M University and worked in a bank wire room before OER.

Lamar Iverson trained Merritt, who was steady under pressure and liked a clean log. As floater Merritt covered the Blue seats through the switch to OER-4 smart cards in March 2012, the June 2012 leap second and Sandy that October.

A floater on the Blue crew covers whatever seat is empty, and in Merritt's time that often meant nights under Leonard Fitch, who had led the Blue nights since 1998. Merritt's logs from those shifts are short, clean and easy to follow.

Off shift Merritt sang in a choir and built models. Merritt left OER on 31 March 2013.
bios.OER-2012-001:
Elena Vasquez was network and regional node engineer from February 2012 to June 2019, following Marcus Bell. Vasquez holds a BS in computer engineering with training in enterprise networking and network security, and came from network operations for a distributed industrial monitoring organization, keeping old regional links running while moving some sites to newer connections.

Vasquez was independent and persistent, and careful about any change that could cut a regional node off. Site-specific exceptions were documented, local and central observations were compared, and failover paths were tested during planned maintenance.

Vasquez drew ten register revisions: the 40 Gb leaf-spine fabric, NET-006 A (May 2013); 10 Gb wavelengths to all eight nodes, NET-002 J, with the new wavelength equipment at each node, NODE-001 D (April 2014); the 100 Gb spine, encryption of every inter-site link and the first encryption drawing, NET-007 A (October 2017); and a separate management network for each site, NET-005 C (February 2018). Vasquez left OER on 30 June 2019.
bios.OER-2012-002:
Trevor Jessup spent six years on the Red day watch: floater from May 2012, then Monitoring from January 2014 to the end of April 2018. Jessup studied business at the University of New Mexico and worked as a data-center operator before OER.

Lorraine Varga trained Jessup, who was reliable on any shift and good at odd faults. Jessup was on the board on 6 July 2015, the first day of the real power grid tile, and for the leap second of 31 December 2016, and watched the first months of the power grid readings settle into a normal daily shape.

Jessup spent nearly two years as the Red floater before taking the day Monitoring desk from Dominic Landry at the start of 2014. Jessup's time on the board included the arrival of the real power grid tile, when the crew had to learn what normal daily demand looked like for each region.

Jessup carpooled with Renata Voigt. Off shift: painting and photography. Jessup left OER on 30 April 2018.
bios.OER-2012-003:
Bruce Norwood held the Red Crew night Correlation seat from September 2012 to the end of January 2014, the first person in the seat after Terrence Garrity's fourteen years. Norwood studied mathematics at the University of Vermont and worked in a bank wire room before OER.

Valerie Tate trained Norwood. Norwood was patient, methodical and good with new staff. Two months in, on 29 October 2012, Norwood was on correlation as Sandy came ashore and Nodes 1 and 2 ran on generator, sorting out which regional reports were outages and which were sites on backup power.

Taking over a desk that one person had held for fourteen years was no small thing, and Norwood did it carefully, keeping Garrity's habits of checking every match against a second source. Norwood was well liked on the night crew for being patient with the newer people.

Off shift Norwood was an amateur radio operator and played guitar. Norwood left OER on 31 January 2014.
bios.OER-2012-004:
Anika Rao owned monitoring automation from December 2012 to April 2018, following Martin Shaw. Rao holds a BS in information technology with scripting and systems operations training, and came from operations automation for a multi-site enterprise, replacing repetitive manual checks with scripts and improving alert handling.

Rao was patient but persistent and questioned any alert that made noise without helping an operator decide what to do. Test cases were kept for each known failure mode, script dependencies were written down, and recurring alerts were reviewed before any threshold was changed.

Rao's years saw the real power grid tile arrive in July 2015 and the collectors and feed handlers move into containers in 2016, and much of the floor's alert wording was tightened in that time. Rao left in April 2018 for an operations engineering role with a larger automation team.
bios.OER-2013-001:
Tobiah Gallo held the Blue Crew night Correlation seat from April to November 2013. Gallo came to OER from production scheduling in Memphis.

Lamar Iverson trained Gallo, who cross-checked records carefully and was reliable overnight. Gallo's months on the night crew were quiet ones by the floor's standards, and Gallo used them to learn the correlation rules thoroughly.

Night correlation on the Blue crew is a desk that rewards patience: most hours are quiet, and the work is checking that what looks quiet really is. Gallo kept the desk's records in good order and handed it on in good shape to Wayne Gutierrez.

Away from work Gallo played chess and quilted. Gallo left OER on 30 November 2013.
bios.OER-2013-002:
Bernadette Dempsey was the Blue Crew floater from June 2013 to the end of June 2014. Dempsey studied information technology at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and worked on a manufacturer's help desk before OER.

Russell Saldana trained Dempsey, who was calm on the phone and steady under pressure. As floater Dempsey covered the Blue seats through the password reset of 9 April 2014, when every account was changed at first login.

Dempsey's year as floater came during a period of change on the Blue crew, with Marcellus Granger and Leonard Fitch both leaving in mid-2014. Dempsey covered the gaps as they came and left clear notes for whoever came next.

Off shift Dempsey cooked for large groups and played softball. Dempsey left OER on 30 June 2014.
bios.OER-2013-003:
Marcus Reed was reliability and performance engineer from July 2013 to December 2020, succeeding Elaine Brooks. Reed holds a B.S. in computer science with training in distributed systems performance, incident analysis and service reliability, and came from enterprise infrastructure operations, investigating slowdowns that crossed storage, compute and network boundaries.

Reed was patient under pressure and persistent about anything left unexplained, and did not trust a green indicator when the measurements behind it disagreed. Measurements were correlated across subsystems, a fault that returned after recovery was recorded as such, and Reed's notes kept "not reproduced" and "resolved" strictly apart.

Reed checked eleven register revisions: the wavelength equipment at the nodes (April 2014), the containerized collectors, SWA-001 H (March 2016), hot aisle containment and the outside-air economizer (September 2016), the modular UPS frames (November 2016), the encrypted Site B links (October 2017), the replacement of generator 1, PWR-005 C (October 2019), and Row F with its liquid cooling, FLR-001 K and MEC-001 E (February 2020). Rachel Kim succeeded Reed.
bios.OER-2013-004:
Martin Ellis was security and system integrity engineer from August 2013 to July 2017, following Kevin Wallace. Ellis holds a B.S. in information systems with training in Unix administration, security auditing and change management, and came from systems administration at a regional data-processing organization, handling account reviews and security exceptions on long-lived Unix systems.

Ellis was patient and skeptical, preferred evidence to assurances, and knew that a hidden dependency can make a simple-looking security change dangerous. Permissions were checked against documented requirements, each exception carried an owner and a review date, and a separate list was kept of access risks still open.

Ellis was in the role on 9 April 2014, when every account was reset after a widely published security flaw and the watch floor changed passwords at first login. Ellis left OER on 31 July 2017, and Andrea Flores took over that October.
bios.OER-2014-001:
Travis Bryce has been on the Red day watch since January 2014: floater for eight years, Correlation from March 2022 and Red Day Lead since May 2023, following Lorraine Varga's twenty-five years on the floor. Bryce grew up in Shreveport, Louisiana, and served four years as an Army signal specialist.

Valerie Tate trained Bryce. Bryce is good at spotting small timing drifts, and as floater learned every seat on the crew. As Lead, Bryce had the floor on 8 April 2024, when the eclipse showed up on the power grid tile in the solar regions from Texas to the Northeast, and has trained much of the current Red crew: Leah Dalton, Naomi Slater, Loretta Spalding and Jordan Madrigal.

Bryce's eight years as floater are the longest anyone has held that job, and they gave Bryce a working knowledge of every Red seat, day and night, before taking any of them. Bryce moved to the day correlation desk in 2022 and to the Lead seat a year later, on the day after Lorraine Varga's last entry.

Off shift Bryce plays board games and takes photographs.
bios.OER-2014-002:
Wayne Gutierrez held the Blue Crew night Correlation seat from January 2014 to the end of April 2019. Gutierrez studied at Fresno State and worked as a hospital systems administrator before OER.

Marvin Poole trained Gutierrez, who remembered past incidents and taught new staff well; Joel Hutchins learned the floor from Gutierrez. Gutierrez worked the night crew through the password reset of April 2014, the leap seconds of 2015 and 2016 and the internet name-service outage of October 2016.

Gutierrez joined the Blue night crew in the same months that Leonard Fitch's long tenure as Lead was ending, and learned the floor under Marvin Poole on Monitoring and Lamar Iverson as Lead. Gutierrez's correlation notes were known for being short and right.

Gutierrez kept a standing lunch with Russell Saldana. Off shift: hiking and fishing. Gutierrez left OER on 30 April 2019.
bios.OER-2014-003:
Eric Matsuda took over interface mapping and data transformation in March 2014, after Nora Whitcomb left, and held the role until October 2019. Matsuda holds a BS in computer science with coursework in distributed systems and database design, and came from integration work at a regional utilities technology provider, linking operational systems, reporting and outside data providers.

Matsuda was pragmatic and independent and disliked transformations that silently dropped unexpected fields. Representative input and output samples were kept, schema changes were tracked, and malformed records and interrupted transfers were tested as well as normal ones. The handling of changed and malformed source records improved a great deal under Matsuda.

Matsuda drew the move of collectors and feed handlers into containers, SWA-001 H (March 2016), and checked six network revisions, including 10 Gb wavelengths to every node (April 2014), the encryption of all inter-site links (October 2017) and the per-site management networks (February 2018). Matsuda left in October 2019 for a senior integration engineering post.
bios.OER-2014-004:
Lyle Jarrett held the Red Crew night Correlation seat from April 2014 to the end of August 2020. Jarrett came to OER from supervising data entry for an insurance carrier.

Valerie Tate trained Jarrett. Jarrett wrote precise log entries and was patient with new staff. Jarrett was on correlation for the leap second of 30 June 2015, when clocks and correlation timing were checked and found normal, and on 6 April 2019, when the GPS week number rollover passed at 18:59:42 local and the GPS clocks and satellite displays stayed normal.

Jarrett's six years on the Red night correlation desk covered the leap seconds of 2015 and 2016, the correlation cluster patch of January 2018 and the GPS week rollover of 2019, all nights when timing mattered more than usual. Jarrett checked the clocks before and after each one.

Off shift Jarrett built models and baked. Jarrett left OER on 31 August 2020.
bios.OER-2014-005:
Antoinette Oakley held the Blue Crew day COMM seat from August 2014 to the end of January 2016. Oakley came to OER from hospital switchboard and telemetry work.

Russell Saldana trained Oakley. Oakley was warm, calm on the phone and good at settling a tense call, the skills a switchboard teaches. Oakley took the Blue day calls through the first year of the real power grid tile, which began in July 2015.

Blue Day COMM had been Nathan Navarro's desk for five years, and Oakley took it on with a switchboard operator's ease. In Oakley's year and a half the regional contacts came to know a voice that was patient and clear and never hurried a caller.

Off shift Oakley was an amateur radio operator and read local history. Oakley left OER on 31 January 2016.
bios.OER-2014-006:
Caden Pacheco held the Blue Crew night COMM seat from August 2014 to the end of September 2018, following Lamar Iverson's fourteen years at that desk. Pacheco studied geography at the University of Toledo and supervised a call center before OER.

Marvin Poole trained Pacheco. Pacheco wrote clear handoffs and read ambiguous data carefully. Pacheco took the night calls through the leap seconds of 2015 and 2016 and the correlation cluster patch window of January 2018.

Blue Night COMM had been held by just two people since the floor opened, Colleen Brannigan and then Lamar Iverson. Pacheco was the third, and kept the habits both of them had built: every call written down, every callback made, nothing in the log that had not been confirmed.

Off shift Pacheco painted and volunteered at a food bank. Pacheco left OER on 30 September 2018.
bios.OER-2014-007:
Yolanda Gilchrist sat Blue Crew day Monitoring from August 2014 to the end of February 2021. Gilchrist grew up in Louisville, Kentucky, and served as a Navy electronics technician.

Gilchrist was a good listener and patient with new staff, and trained Hugo Dawson. Gilchrist was on the board on 21 October 2016, when an internet name-service outage cut five external feeds while regional node data kept flowing; on 21 August 2017, when the eclipse crossed the power grid tile region by region; on 13 January 2018, during the correlation cluster patch window; and in February 2021, when the Texas freeze put Node 4 on generator and the crew rechecked every hour.

Gilchrist's six and a half years on the Blue day board made Gilchrist one of the most experienced Monitoring operators of that decade, and Gilchrist was often the person new staff were seated beside in their first weeks.

Off shift Gilchrist played board games and was an amateur radio operator. Gilchrist left OER on 28 February 2021.
bios.OER-2014-008:
Lorna Barlow spent nine years on the Blue day watch: floater from September 2014, then COMM from October 2016 to the end of August 2023. Barlow studied at the University of Texas at El Paso and led IT support for a school district before OER.

Russell Saldana trained Barlow, and Barlow trained Ezra Blackwell and Savannah Stafford. Barlow was on the COMM desk for the internet name-service outage of 21 October 2016, recording each late feed; for the 2017 eclipse; the February 2021 Texas freeze; the first day of full seating after the pandemic precautions, 7 June 2021; the first morning of the LED wall, 11 April 2022; and the first day of the AI incident tile, 27 March 2023.

Barlow was calm on the phone, precise in the log and the unofficial host of the break room. Off shift: softball and crossword puzzles. Barlow left OER on 31 August 2023.
bios.OER-2015-001:
Daniel Mercer ran configuration and release from March 2015 to August 2019, following Michael Turner. Mercer holds a B.S. in information systems with training in Unix administration, version control and IT change management, and came from systems operations engineering at a regional data-processing organization, resolving differences between approved packages and production installs.

Mercer respected change control but challenged any procedure that added paperwork without adding reliability. A personal release checklist recorded exact version identifiers, copies of known-good packages were kept, and any manual step was noted.

Mercer checked the dense multicore support servers, RCK-04 F (August 2015), the container hosts for collectors and feed handlers, RCK-05 D (March 2016), and object storage for the archive, RCK-02 J (June 2016), with tape kept as the offline copy, and drew the matching inventory, INV-001 H. Mercer left OER on 31 August 2019, and Christopher Nguyen took over that November.
bios.OER-2015-002:
David Chen looked after OER's Linux and virtual infrastructure from April 2015 to December 2020. Chen holds a BS in computer science with training in Linux administration and enterprise virtualization, and came from infrastructure engineering for a multi-site enterprise: servers, virtual machines, storage and hardware lifecycle.

Chen was steady under pressure and favored repeatable maintenance and controlled change over rushed upgrades. Host and dependency inventories were kept, maintenance outcomes were recorded, and application and service health were checked after every infrastructure change. Chen standardized the checks the team still runs after maintenance.

Chen signed 20 register revisions: drawing the dense multicore servers (2015), the container hosts and object storage (2016), hot aisle containment, FLR-001 J (September 2016), the modular UPS frames (November 2016), the replacement of generator 1 (October 2019) and Row F for accelerator nodes with its liquid cooling, FLR-001 K (February 2020); and approving the network revisions of 2017-18 between network engineers. Chen left in December 2020 for a senior infrastructure role, and Stephanie Walsh took over.
bios.OER-2015-003:
Simone Blake was data quality and correlation engineer from April 2015 to December 2019, following Alan Pierce. Blake holds a BS in applied mathematics and a graduate certificate in data analysis, and came from a distributed environmental monitoring network, reconciling observations from instruments with different sampling intervals and error behavior.

Blake was thoughtful and independent and could challenge an assumption without making a disagreement personal. Time windows and source behavior were checked before any threshold was changed, and examples of both successful and failed correlations were kept side by side.

Blake improved how OER handles timing differences between sources and correlations that remain uncertain, work that mattered more as the number of outside feeds grew and as the floor began reading regional power demand from national data in 2015. Blake left in December 2019 for a research analytics position.
bios.OER-2016-001:
Calvin Brooks has been OER's database and archive administrator since April 2016, following Sonia Patel. Brooks holds a BS in information technology with training in storage systems and data integrity, and came from database reliability at a distributed monitoring service, looking after historical records and aging archive formats.

Brooks is conservative with historical records and will not discard an old format or overwrite an uncertain copy before comparing them. Archive manifests are recorded, checksums and record counts are verified, notes are kept on obsolete formats and what depends on them, and a restore is tested before an archive is called healthy. Some of OER's oldest records have poorly documented formats, and Brooks has preserved them carefully.

Brooks drew model-based correlation, SWA-001 J (February 2020), and checked the move of collection processing to the nodes before transfer, SWA-001 K and SWA-002 E (September 2024). The archive moved to object storage the year Brooks arrived and now keeps immutable copies.
bios.OER-2016-002:
Heather Nolan sat Red Crew night Monitoring from April 2016 to the end of February 2019, the first person at the desk after Angela Vail's thirteen years, and the one who found the lamp Vail left behind. Nolan studied communication at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga and worked as a trucking dispatcher before OER.

Nolan cross-checked records carefully and was always on time. Nolan worked the Red nights through the leap second of December 2016 and the correlation cluster patch of January 2018.

The Red night Monitoring desk had been Angela Vail's for thirteen years, and Nolan inherited both the seat and the lamp that came with it. Nolan worked the Red nights under Valerie Tate and then Whitney Haddad, and kept the desk's log exact.

Off shift Nolan went camping and did woodworking. Nolan left OER on 28 February 2019.
bios.OER-2016-003:
Beverly Ashby has been on the Blue Crew night watch since October 2016: floater for two years, Monitoring from November 2018 and Blue Night Lead since December 2019. Ashby studied physics at Georgia Southern University and worked in cloud operations before OER.

Marvin Poole trained Ashby, and Ashby has trained much of the current Blue night crew: Danielle Quarles, Tyrone Hobart and Alicia Winslow. Ashby led the night crew through the pandemic precautions of 2020 and 2021, and on 10 May 2024 had the floor when the geomagnetic storm reached the highest level and the crew rechecked GPS status every hour.

Ashby spent two years as the Blue floater, then a year on night Monitoring, before taking the Lead seat from Marvin Poole in December 2019. Within months the floor was working under pandemic precautions, and Ashby kept the Blue nights fully staffed through the whole of it.

Ashby is calm on the phone and always tinkering. Off shift: baking and softball.
bios.OER-2017-001:
Lila Morgan has owned communications and external feeds since May 2017, following Evan Brooks. Morgan holds a BS in information systems with training in network operations and distributed monitoring, and came from a multi-site technical operations environment, supporting outside telemetry, provider-managed links and the move from older transports to internet-delivered feeds.

Morgan is steady and independent and skeptical of vendor assurances without end-to-end evidence, and will keep an awkward but reliable interface until its replacement has proven itself. The old interface notes are kept, provider maintenance notices are checked against the outages actually seen, and workarounds are written down so newer staff do not mistake them for design.

Nine years on, Morgan knows the history of most of OER's feed providers better than anyone. Morgan has been in the role for the 2019 GPS week rollover, the arrival of the AI incident tile in March 2023 and the space weather storm of May 2024.
bios.OER-2017-002:
Logan Kaplan held the Red Crew day Correlation seat from September 2017 to the end of March 2018, following Theresa Valdez. Kaplan came to OER from a university data center.

Kaplan was calm on the phone and alert to small timing drifts. Kaplan's months on the Red day crew included the correlation cluster patch window of 13 January 2018, when correlation was expected to run up to ten percent slower afterward, and Kaplan watched the timing closely to confirm it stayed within that.

Kaplan's months on the Red day correlation desk fell between Theresa Valdez's long tenure and Camila Satterfield's year, and Kaplan kept the desk's notes in good shape for the next person.

Off shift Kaplan played chess and cooked for large groups. Kaplan left OER on 31 March 2018.
bios.OER-2017-003:
Andrea Flores was security and system integrity engineer from October 2017 to March 2022, following Martin Ellis. Flores holds a B.S. in information technology with continuing education in security operations, vulnerability assessment and incident handling, and came from infrastructure support at a large regional information-services organization.

Flores was calm, analytical and pragmatic: weaknesses had to be fixed, but an untested security change could cause a wider outage than the weakness itself. Open findings were tracked by owner and review date, each proposed fix was checked for its effect on the regional nodes, and recurring exceptions were noted.

Flores drew SEC-001 G, the OER-5 mobile credential and card (April 2021), and handled security through the encrypted inter-site links of 2017 and the separated management networks of 2018. Flores left OER on 31 March 2022, and Daniel Price took over in May.
bios.OER-2018-001:
Patricia Greene served as systems architect and technical lead from March 2018 to August 2022, after an eight-month vacancy following Michael Grant. Greene holds an MS in software engineering and a BS in computer science, and came from enterprise architecture for a distributed infrastructure and data-services organization, running design reviews and assessing modernization risk.

Greene was patient but firm and skeptical of redesigns that lacked a rollback plan. Architecture decision records were kept for every significant change, a list was maintained of dependencies nobody had documented, and each team was asked which systems a proposed change would touch.

Greene approved 16 register revisions: the replacement of generator 1 (October 2019), Row F for accelerator nodes and model-based correlation (February 2020), the OER-5 mobile credential (April 2021), the database servers and 60 PB archive (May 2021), the modular UPS (June 2021), the direct-view LED wall on the watch floor and at Site B, FLR-002 F (April 2022), and the 400 Gb spine (August 2022). Greene left in August 2022 for an enterprise architecture leadership post, and Adrian Cole succeeded Greene.
bios.OER-2018-002:
Whitney Haddad led the Red Crew night watch from May 2018 to the end of August 2019, following Valerie Tate. Haddad studied physics at Wichita State University and supervised data entry for an insurance carrier before OER.

Renata Voigt trained Haddad, and Haddad trained Leo Halloran. Haddad was quiet, watchful and careful with ambiguous data. Haddad was the Lead on 6 April 2019, when the GPS week number rollover passed at 18:59:42 local and the crew logged that the GPS clocks and satellite status displays were normal.

Haddad took the Red night Lead seat from Valerie Tate in May 2018 and held it for more than a year, with Renata Voigt still at the COMM desk and Lyle Jarrett on correlation. Haddad's logs are quiet and careful and say exactly what was checked.

Off shift Haddad painted and quilted. Haddad left OER on 31 August 2019.
bios.OER-2018-003:
Camila Satterfield held the Red Crew day Correlation seat from August 2018 to the end of June 2019. Satterfield studied business at the University of Alabama at Birmingham and worked in production scheduling before OER.

Reuben Schaefer trained Satterfield. Satterfield read ambiguous data carefully and wrote precise log entries, and kept the Red day correlation desk steady through a year of turnover on the crew.

Satterfield's year on correlation came during a period of change on the Red day crew, with Selena Crowe newly on Monitoring and Reuben Schaefer at COMM. Satterfield kept the correlation records in good order and handed the desk on to Brandon Chastain.

Off shift Satterfield baked and sang in a choir. Satterfield left OER on 30 June 2019.
bios.OER-2018-004:
Selena Crowe sat Red Crew day Monitoring for seven years, from September 2018 to the end of October 2025. Crowe studied communication at Boise State University and worked a hospital switchboard and telemetry desk before OER.

Reuben Schaefer trained Crowe. Crowe read everything twice and was calm on the phone. Crowe was on the board on 16 March 2020, the first morning of pandemic precautions, and on 8 April 2024, when the eclipse dipped the power grid readings in the solar regions from Texas to the Northeast; the log for that afternoon reads forecast, no action.

Crowe's seven years at the Red day Monitoring desk spanned the pandemic years, the return to full seating, the new LED wall in 2022 and the first years of the AI incident tile. Crowe handed the desk to Loretta Spalding at the end of 2025.

Off shift Crowe baked and did woodworking. Crowe left OER on 31 October 2025.
bios.OER-2018-005:
Courtney Marlow has held the Blue Crew night COMM seat since November 2018. Marlow came to OER from training public-safety communicators, and still brings a trainer's habits to the desk.

Marvin Poole trained Marlow, and Marlow has become the Blue crew's main trainer: Melissa Ramsey, Vincent Knox, Isaac Cordero and Ellis Gentry all learned the floor from Marlow. Marlow took the night calls through the pandemic precautions of 2020 and 2021, and on 10 May 2024 was at the COMM desk during the geomagnetic storm.

Blue Night COMM has had only four regular holders since 1998, and Marlow's eight years make Marlow the second-longest in that seat after Lamar Iverson. The newer staff on the Blue crew tend to describe the floor's procedures in Marlow's words.

Marlow writes clear handoffs. Off shift: amateur radio and model building.
bios.OER-2018-006:
Joel Hutchins was the Blue Crew floater from November 2018 to the end of November 2019. Hutchins studied at Montana State University Billings and worked at an alarm-monitoring station before OER.

Wayne Gutierrez trained Hutchins. Hutchins was calm, dry and good at organizing a shift. As floater Hutchins covered the Blue seats through the GPS week number rollover of April 2019 and the changes in the Blue night crew that year.

As floater Hutchins worked whichever seat was empty and learned the Blue night routine under Marvin Poole in Poole's last year as Lead. Hutchins's notes were brief and easy to pick up.

Off shift Hutchins read local history and baked. Hutchins left OER on 30 November 2019.
bios.OER-2019-001:
Leo Halloran sat Red Crew night Monitoring from May 2019 to the end of October 2022. Halloran grew up in Salt Lake City, Utah, and served four years as an Army signal specialist.

Whitney Haddad trained Halloran. Halloran remembered past incidents in detail and organized a shift well. Halloran worked the Red nights through the pandemic precautions of 2020 and 2021, the Texas freeze of February 2021 and the first months of the LED wall in 2022.

Halloran took the Red night Monitoring desk after Heather Nolan and held it for three and a half years under Cecil Eaton, with Renata Voigt still at COMM. Halloran's handoffs were known for listing what had changed on the board overnight in the order it changed.

Halloran carpooled with Lorraine Varga and is a friend of Renata Voigt. Off shift: birdwatching and fishing. Halloran left OER on 31 October 2022.
bios.OER-2019-002:
Danielle Quarles has held the Blue Crew night Correlation seat since June 2019. Quarles came to OER from production scheduling.

Beverly Ashby trained Quarles. Quarles is calm on the phone and always tinkering, with the humor to keep a night crew going. Quarles worked the night correlation desk through the pandemic precautions of 2020 and 2021, and on 10 May 2024 was on correlation during the geomagnetic storm, matching GPS and space weather reports while the crew rechecked GPS status every hour.

Quarles has held the Blue night correlation desk for more than seven years, longer than anyone since Gail Everett. Quarles and Beverly Ashby have worked the same Blue nights for most of that time, and the crew's routine reflects both of them.

Off shift Quarles plays board games and cooks for a crowd.
bios.OER-2019-003:
Brandon Chastain held the Red Crew day Correlation seat from August 2019 to the end of February 2022. Chastain studied mathematics at Worcester State University and worked in a security operations center before OER.

Chastain cross-checked records carefully and wrote clear handoffs. Chastain was on the correlation desk on 16 March 2020, the first morning of pandemic precautions, when every other console was used and the handover went by phone bridge, and worked the Red day crew through the months that followed until full seating returned in June 2021.

Chastain's background in a security operations center helped on a floor where more of the work was now about feeds and services as well as regional sites, and Chastain was often the person who could explain why an outside feed had gone quiet.

Off shift Chastain went camping and was an amateur radio operator. Chastain left OER on 28 February 2022.
bios.OER-2019-004:
Cecil Eaton led the Red Crew night watch for nearly seven years, from October 2019 to the end of August 2026. Eaton came from a telephone company, first as an operator and then supervising customer service.

Renata Voigt trained Eaton, and Voigt took the Lead seat when Eaton left. Eaton picked up new tools quickly and trained Tiffany Quade, Krista Stroud and Tyler Rawlings. Eaton led the Red nights through the pandemic precautions of 2020, the Texas freeze of February 2021, the first months of the LED wall and the first year of the AI incident tile.

Eaton took the Red night Lead seat from Whitney Haddad and held it longer than anyone since Valerie Tate. Eaton's crew included Renata Voigt at COMM throughout, Morgan Hammond on correlation and, from 2023, Krista Stroud on Monitoring.

Off shift Eaton cooked for large groups and ran. Eaton left OER on 31 August 2026.
bios.OER-2019-005:
Christopher Nguyen has run configuration and release since November 2019, following Daniel Mercer. Nguyen holds a B.S. in computer science with training in Linux administration, configuration management and deployment automation, and came from systems engineering for enterprise infrastructure releases.

Nguyen is analytical and quietly persistent, favors repeatable procedures over informal assurances, and is careful about automating changes to poorly documented older systems. Deployment scripts are versioned, hashes and revision identifiers are checked, and any manual step outside the standard procedure is recorded.

Nguyen has signed twelve register revisions: the accelerator nodes and their inventory (February 2020), the OER-5 credential (April 2021), the database servers and 60 PB archive with RCK-01 F, which keeps the line "A01-A03 retained, powered" (May 2021), the 2U server chassis (2023), the retirement of Row C (June 2024), the node processing servers, INV-002 E (September 2024), and the 120 PB archive with immutable copies, RCK-02 L (March 2025).
bios.OER-2020-001:
Jenna Sutton joined the Blue Crew in January 2020, was floater for nearly five years and has held the Blue day Correlation seat since October 2024. Sutton holds an associate degree in computer networking and came to OER from a security operations center.

Sutton started two months before the pandemic precautions of March 2020 and learned all four Blue seats in the years of split seating that followed. Sutton reads every report twice, writes some of the clearest handoff notes on the floor and is the one the crew hands a tense call to. Sutton trained Sierra Renner and Taylor Thatcher.

Off shift Sutton gardens and rides a bicycle.
bios.OER-2020-002:
Tyrone Hobart sat Blue Crew night Monitoring from January to the end of June 2020. Hobart studied geography at Eastern Washington University and worked at an alarm-monitoring station before OER.

Beverly Ashby trained Hobart, who always asked for the second source. Hobart's months on the night crew covered the start of the pandemic precautions, when the floor kept every shift fully staffed and cleaned between shifts.

Hobart's short time on the floor was spent on a Blue night crew led by Beverly Ashby, with Courtney Marlow at COMM and Danielle Quarles on correlation. Hobart's notes from those months are careful and complete.

Off shift Hobart played guitar and gardened. Hobart left OER on 30 June 2020.
bios.OER-2020-003:
Hugo Dawson held the Blue Crew day Correlation seat from February 2020 to the end of November 2021, following Russell Saldana's twelve years at the desk. Dawson studied communication at the University of Kentucky and worked for a transportation agency before OER.

Yolanda Gilchrist trained Dawson. Dawson was a good listener and calm on the phone. Dawson was on correlation on 15 February 2021, when the Texas freeze put Node 4 on generator and rotating outages showed on the power grid tile, and on 7 June 2021, the first day of full seating on the floor.

Dawson took the Blue day correlation desk after twelve years of Russell Saldana and kept it for nearly two years, including most of the pandemic precautions, when every other console was used and handovers went by phone bridge.

Off shift Dawson went camping and built models. Dawson left OER on 30 November 2021.
bios.OER-2020-004:
Owen Clarke has owned monitoring and automation since February 2020, after an extended vacancy following Anika Rao. Clarke holds a BS in computer engineering with training in monitoring platforms and infrastructure automation, and came from site reliability and monitoring work for a distributed infrastructure service.

Clarke is technically curious and pragmatic and prefers improvements that do not unsettle dependable older routines. Clarke looks after both OER's long-running jobs and its newer health checks, tracks silent failures and stale outputs, tests jobs after any change to what they depend on, and writes notes on an undocumented script before touching it.

Clarke's years have included the pandemic precautions of 2020, the Monitoring Grid's newer feeds, the AI incident tile of March 2023 and the morning of 19 July 2024, when desk PCs failed after a vendor update and the console systems kept running. Detecting a stale result, not just a failed one, has been Clarke's main contribution.
bios.OER-2020-005:
Thomas Reed has been network and regional node engineer since March 2020, after a six-month vacancy following Elena Vasquez. Reed holds a BS in computer networks with training in network observability and infrastructure resilience, and came from network reliability work for a distributed infrastructure provider, investigating intermittent connectivity and routing instability at remote sites.

Reed is pragmatic and vigilant and does not trust a single monitoring signal when independent paths disagree. Regional and central telemetry are compared, recurring path instability is tracked, and the dependencies between node connectivity and data collection are written down, so the floor can now tell a network failure from a local collection failure.

Reed has drawn eight register revisions: the LED wall at Site B (April 2022), the 400 Gb spine, NET-001 K and NET-006 C (August 2022), private 100 Gb wavelengths to every site, NET-002 L (March 2023), shorter key rotation and a new cipher suite, NET-007 B (January 2024), the node processing rack, NODE-001 E (September 2024), and 800 Gb core links, NET-001 L (November 2025).
bios.OER-2020-006:
Alicia Winslow sat Blue Crew night Monitoring from July 2020 to the end of January 2021. Winslow studied engineering technology at Sacramento State and worked a hospital switchboard and telemetry desk before OER.

Beverly Ashby trained Winslow, who was good at odd faults and tense calls. Winslow's months on the night crew fell entirely within the pandemic precautions, with split seating and cleaning between shifts.

Winslow learned the Blue night board while the floor was working under the pandemic precautions, sitting at every other console and handing over by phone bridge, and was trusted on the desk alone within weeks.

Off shift Winslow sang in a choir and rode a bicycle. Winslow left OER on 31 January 2021.
bios.OER-2020-007:
Rebecca Lin has been data integration and interface engineer since July 2020, after an eight-month vacancy following Eric Matsuda. Lin holds a BS in computer science with graduate coursework in information systems integration, and came from a regional infrastructure monitoring provider, maintaining pipelines between operational telemetry, outside feeds and older reporting systems.

Lin is pragmatic and observant and cautious about replacing a stable older interface without proving the new one behaves the same. Representative payloads are kept, schema and provider changes are recorded, and duplicate delivery, partial failure and stale data are all tested. Lin looks after the newer API connections and the inherited batch transfers alike.

Lin drew the move of collection processing to the nodes before transfer, SWA-001 K and SWA-002 E (September 2024), and has checked the network revisions of the same years, from the 400 Gb spine (2022) and private wavelengths (2023) to the 800 Gb core links of November 2025.
bios.OER-2020-008:
Ibrahim Shah was data quality and correlation engineer from September 2020 to February 2025. Shah holds an MS in computer science specializing in distributed systems and information retrieval, and came from data fusion for a large monitoring platform, reconciling events from independent systems with incomplete and sometimes contradictory observations.

Shah was highly methodical, distrusted undocumented rules of thumb, and would leave a correlation open rather than invent certainty. Regression cases were kept for unusual correlations, source changes were reviewed for side effects, and the reason for every threshold was written down.

Shah arrived months after correlation moved to a model-based method in February 2020, and brought formal testing discipline to it, along with clear records of confidence and source provenance. Shah's years covered the Texas freeze of 2021, the AI incident tile of 2023 and the eclipse and geomagnetic storm of spring 2024. Shah left in February 2025 for a senior role in another monitoring program.
bios.OER-2020-009:
Morgan Hammond held the Red Crew night Correlation seat from September 2020 to the end of April 2025. Hammond came to OER from a bank wire room.

Renata Voigt trained Hammond. Hammond wrote precise log entries and was patient with new staff. Hammond worked the Red nights through the Texas freeze of February 2021, the first months of the LED wall in 2022, the first year of the AI incident tile and the geomagnetic storm of May 2024.

Hammond's four and a half years on the Red night correlation desk followed Lyle Jarrett's six, and Hammond handed it on to Tyler Rawlings in 2025. Hammond's correlation notes are short, exact and dated to the minute.

Off shift Hammond did crossword puzzles and sang in a choir. Hammond left OER on 30 April 2025.
bios.OER-2020-010:
Leah Dalton held the Red Crew day COMM seat from December 2020 to the end of July 2024, following Reuben Schaefer. Dalton grew up in Tucson, Arizona, and served four years as an Army signal specialist.

Travis Bryce trained Dalton, who was hard to rattle, organized a shift well and wrote clear handoffs. Dalton was at the COMM desk on 8 April 2024, when the eclipse crossed the power grid tile, and worked the Red days through the return to full seating in 2021 and the first months of the LED wall.

Dalton's time at the Red day COMM desk covered the last year of the pandemic precautions, the return to full seating, the LED wall and the first year of the AI incident tile. Dalton handed the desk on to Tiffany Quade in 2024.

Off shift Dalton hiked and ran. Dalton left OER on 31 July 2024.
bios.OER-2021-001:
Rachel Kim has been reliability and performance engineer since January 2021, succeeding Marcus Reed. Kim holds a B.S. in computer engineering with training in site reliability engineering, performance instrumentation and incident response, and came from production reliability work in a large interconnected services environment.

Kim is observant and quietly skeptical and questions a reassuring summary when the measurements underneath are still abnormal. Every note carries timestamps and comparison points, the difference between a service being restored and a system being fully recovered is always recorded, and unexplained deviations are flagged without overstating them.

Kim has checked seven register revisions: the modular UPS (June 2021), the LED wall on the watch floor and at Site B (April 2022), the automated Site B checklist steps, SITE-B-002 F (January 2024), the retirement of Row C (June 2024), the node processing rack (September 2024) and the replacement of the UPS battery strings, PWR-001 J (March 2025).
bios.OER-2021-002:
Stephanie Walsh has looked after OER's servers and infrastructure since January 2021, following David Chen. Walsh holds a BS in information technology with training in Linux systems engineering, virtualization and infrastructure resilience, and came from a distributed technical services organization, maintaining Linux and virtual workloads and chasing intermittent failures.

Walsh is pragmatic and observant, prefers step-by-step modernization, and is cautious about undocumented dependencies in long-running systems. Host and dependency inventories are kept, recurring faults are recorded, storage, services and recent job results are checked after maintenance, and each older exception is documented before it is changed.

Walsh has drawn twelve register revisions: the database servers and 60 PB archive (May 2021), with RCK-01 F keeping A01-A03 retained and powered; the modular UPS (June 2021); the re-spaced console rows for the LED wall, FLR-002 F (April 2022); the 2U server chassis (2023); the retirement of Row C and the extension of Row F (June 2024); and the 120 PB archive and new UPS batteries (March 2025).
bios.OER-2021-003:
Melissa Ramsey has sat Blue Crew night Monitoring since March 2021. Ramsey studied geography at the University of Alaska Anchorage and worked as a hospital systems administrator before OER.

Courtney Marlow trained Ramsey. Ramsey is reliable overnight and careful with ambiguous data. Ramsey was on the board on 10 May 2024, when the geomagnetic storm reached the highest level and the night crew rechecked GPS status every hour, and has watched the Blue nights from the new LED wall since April 2022.

Ramsey sits a Blue night crew led by Beverly Ashby, with Courtney Marlow at COMM and Danielle Quarles on correlation, a crew that has worked together for years. Ramsey's handoffs list what changed on the board in the order it changed.

Off shift Ramsey fishes and fixes old cars.
bios.OER-2021-004:
Ezra Blackwell sat Blue Crew day Monitoring from November 2021 to the end of February 2024. Blackwell studied mathematics at the University of Tulsa and worked on a cable company's network before OER.

Lorna Barlow trained Blackwell. Blackwell remembered past incidents and taught new staff well. Blackwell was on the board on 11 April 2022, the first morning of the LED wall, when every console position moved and the crew checked seat cards, and on 27 March 2023, the first day of the AI incident tile.

Blackwell's time on the Blue day board fell between Yolanda Gilchrist's long tenure and Taylor Thatcher's arrival, and covered the move to the LED wall and the first year of the AI incident tile.

Off shift Blackwell fixed old cars and played chess. Blackwell left OER on 29 February 2024.
bios.OER-2022-001:
Savannah Stafford held the Blue Crew day Correlation seat from February 2022 to the end of May 2024. Stafford studied psychology at Jackson State University and worked in records and analysis for a state agency before OER.

Lorna Barlow trained Stafford, who always asked for the second source. Stafford was on correlation on 11 April 2022, the first morning of the LED wall, and on 27 March 2023, when the AI incident tile went into service and the crew started applying the new rules to AI incident reports.

Stafford's time at the Blue day correlation desk came between Hugo Dawson and Jenna Sutton, and Stafford's notes from those years are careful about which reports came from where.

Off shift Stafford played softball and painted. Stafford left OER on 31 May 2024.
bios.OER-2022-002:
Daniel Price has been security and system integrity engineer since May 2022, following Andrea Flores. Price holds a Bachelor of Applied Science in information technology with training in access governance, vulnerability management and incident response, and came from enterprise infrastructure operations, maintaining security controls on mixed-generation Unix and Linux systems.

Price regularly inherited undocumented permissions, unsupported hosts and exceptions that had outlived their owners, and is wary of calling an old system secure just because it is still running. Account ownership and last-use records are checked, OER's exception register is kept current, and each deferred fix is written down with its operational reason.

Price prefers controlled remediation to sweeping change. Price's years have included shorter key rotation and a new cipher suite on the inter-site links (January 2024) and the morning of 19 July 2024, when desk PCs and the badge station failed after a vendor update and had to be recovered one by one.
bios.OER-2022-003:
Tiffany Quade spent three and a half years on the Red day watch: floater from May 2022, then COMM from September 2024 to the end of November 2025. Quade studied psychology at UNC Charlotte and worked a hospital switchboard and telemetry desk before OER.

Cecil Eaton trained Quade. Quade remembered past incidents and could calm a tense call. As floater Quade covered all four Red seats through the first years of the LED wall and the AI incident tile, and through the busy spring of 2024: the eclipse in April and the geomagnetic storm in May.

Quade spent more than two years as the Red floater before taking the day COMM desk from Leah Dalton in September 2024, and handed it on to Cody Hendry at the end of 2025.

Off shift Quade baked and was an amateur radio operator. Quade left OER on 30 November 2025.
bios.OER-2022-004:
Adrian Cole has been OER's systems architect and technical lead since September 2022, succeeding Patricia Greene. Cole holds an MS in computer science and a BS in computer engineering, and came from principal architecture work on a long-running operational technology platform, planning compatibility across older services, newer infrastructure and data systems with incomplete design records.

Cole is patient and curious, resists early conclusions, and avoids changes that would erase evidence of how a system actually behaves. Current behavior is compared with historical design records, unexplained dependencies are documented, and before-and-after evidence is kept for every architecture change. Cole has gathered the scattered dependency records into one set.

Cole has approved 15 register revisions: private 100 Gb wavelengths to every site (March 2023), the 2U server chassis (September 2023), the new cipher suite (January 2024), the retirement of Row C (June 2024), collection processing at the nodes and the node processing rack (September 2024), the 120 PB archive with immutable copies and the new UPS batteries (March 2025), and the 800 Gb core links (November 2025).
bios.OER-2023-001:
Krista Stroud has sat Red Crew night Monitoring since February 2023. Stroud studied information systems at Colorado State University and worked as a data-center operator before OER.

Cecil Eaton trained Stroud. Stroud is good at spotting small timing drifts and organizing a shift. Stroud joined the Red nights weeks before the AI incident tile went into service, and was on the floor through the geomagnetic storm of May 2024, watching the GPS status on the wall every hour.

Stroud's time on the Red nights has been under two Leads, Cecil Eaton and then Renata Voigt, who has been on that crew since 1998. Stroud's handoff notes are brief, timed and easy to pick up.

Off shift Stroud goes camping and volunteers at a food bank.
bios.OER-2023-002:
Naomi Slater held the Red Crew day Correlation seat from June 2023 to the end of January 2026. Slater studied information systems at the University of Akron and worked in site-reliability engineering before OER.

Travis Bryce trained Slater, who always asked for the second source and was good at odd faults. Slater was on correlation on 8 April 2024, when the eclipse dipped the power grid readings from Texas to the Northeast, and on 19 July 2024, when desk PCs failed after a vendor update and the crew worked from the console systems until Engineering cleared them.

Slater's time at the Red day correlation desk followed Travis Bryce's own year there, and Slater handed the desk on to Mason Rafferty in 2026.

Off shift Slater was an amateur radio operator and fished. Slater left OER on 31 January 2026.
bios.OER-2024-001:
Sierra Renner held the Blue Crew day COMM seat from January 2024 to the end of April 2025. Renner studied business at Ohio State University and supervised a call center before OER.

Jenna Sutton trained Renner, who learned new tools quickly. Renner was at the COMM desk on 19 July 2024, when the desk PCs and the badge station failed after a vendor update; the crew worked from the console systems only, and Renner kept the outside calls moving until Engineering cleared the desks.

Renner's time on the Blue day COMM desk followed Lorna Barlow's seven years, and Renner handed it on to Declan Fontaine in 2025.

Off shift Renner rode a bicycle and played guitar. Renner left OER on 30 April 2025.
bios.OER-2024-002:
Taylor Thatcher has sat Blue Crew day Monitoring since June 2024. Thatcher came to OER from hospital switchboard and telemetry work.

Jenna Sutton trained Thatcher. Thatcher is quiet and watchful and remembers past incidents in detail. Seven weeks into the job, on 19 July 2024, Thatcher was on the board when the desk PCs and the badge station failed after a vendor update, and watched the console systems alone until Engineering cleared the desks.

Thatcher took the Blue day board after Ezra Blackwell and sits with Craig Lowry, who has led the Blue days since 2007, and Jenna Sutton on correlation.

Thatcher keeps a standing lunch with Craig Lowry. Off shift: cycling and amateur radio.
bios.OER-2024-003:
Vincent Knox was the Blue Crew floater from October 2024 to the end of March 2025. Knox studied computer science at the University of Minnesota Duluth and worked in telehealth support before OER.

Courtney Marlow trained Knox, who was good at odd faults and tense calls. As floater Knox covered the Blue seats through the winter of 2024-25, after Jenna Sutton moved to the day correlation desk. Knox covered all four Blue seats in turn, day and night, during a winter with several new faces on the crew.

Knox's time as floater was short, but Knox learned the Blue night routine under Beverly Ashby and handed on clear notes.

Off shift Knox played softball and gardened. Knox left OER on 31 March 2025.
bios.OER-2024-004:
Loretta Spalding joined the Red Crew as floater in November 2024 and has sat Red day Monitoring since December 2025, following Selena Crowe's seven years at the desk. Spalding came to OER from a university data center.

Travis Bryce trained Spalding. Spalding is alert to small timing drifts and calm on a tense call, with a dry wit, and already trains others: Mason Rafferty learned the correlation desk from Spalding. As floater Spalding learned all four Red seats in a year.

Spalding sits on a Red day crew led by Travis Bryce, with Cody Hendry at COMM and Mason Rafferty on correlation, and is often the person the newest staff turn to with a question about the board.

Off shift Spalding plays board games and takes photographs.
bios.OER-2025-001:
