Declan Fontaine has held the Blue Crew day COMM seat since June 2025, following Sierra Renner. Fontaine studied psychology at Buffalo State and worked in telehealth support before OER.

Fontaine is calm on the phone and alert to small timing drifts, and has settled quickly into a seat where most of the job is saying only what has been confirmed. Fontaine works alongside Craig Lowry, the Blue Day Lead since 2007, and Jenna Sutton on correlation.

Declan Fontaine is the newest holder of a seat that Craig Lowry held for seven years and Lorna Barlow for seven more, and has learned the regional contact list quickly.

Off shift Fontaine gardens and volunteers at a food bank.
bios.OER-2025-002:
Isaac Cordero was the Blue Crew floater from June 2025 to the end of September 2026. Cordero studied business at SUNY Albany and worked as a data-center operator before OER.

Courtney Marlow trained Cordero. Cordero was steady under pressure, always tinkering and precise in the log. As floater Cordero covered all four Blue seats, day and night, for more than a year, and handed the floater's binder to Ellis Gentry.

Cordero's time as floater covered the change of Red night Lead from Cecil Eaton to Renata Voigt in the autumn of 2026, when several seats changed hands at once.

Off shift Cordero baked and rode a bicycle. Cordero left OER on 30 September 2026.
bios.OER-2025-003:
Tyler Rawlings has held the Red Crew night Correlation seat since July 2025, following Morgan Hammond. Rawlings studied physics at the University of Illinois Springfield and worked in a bank wire room before OER.

Cecil Eaton trained Rawlings. Rawlings is quiet, watchful and careful with records, and sits on a night crew now led by Renata Voigt, who has been on the Red nights since the floor opened.

Rawlings took the desk from Morgan Hammond and keeps the correlation notes in the same short, dated form that Terrence Garrity started on that desk in 1998.

Off shift Rawlings gardens and fixes old cars.
bios.OER-2026-001:
Cody Hendry has held the Red Crew day COMM seat since January 2026, following Tiffany Quade. Hendry studied business at Cleveland State University and worked as a county 911 dispatcher before OER, the same path that brought Joanne Tillman to the floor in 1998.

Hendry is good at settling a tense call and remembers past incidents. Hendry works with Travis Bryce, the Red Day Lead, and Loretta Spalding on Monitoring, and is still learning the floor's long list of regional contacts.

The Red day COMM seat was Tillman's for its first four years, and Hendry has been told about that more than once.

Off shift Hendry gardens and watches birds.
bios.OER-2026-002:
Jordan Madrigal has been the Red Crew floater since February 2026. Madrigal came to OER from a manufacturer's help desk.

Travis Bryce trained Madrigal. Madrigal is patient and methodical and already writes clear handoffs. As floater Madrigal is learning all four Red seats, day and night, and covers whichever one is empty, the job that has trained many of the floor's leads. Madrigal came on in the same year as Cody Hendry and Mason Rafferty, part of a new generation on the Red days.

Madrigal has worked under Travis Bryce, who held the Red floater's job for eight years, and gets advice on the job from the person who knows it best.

Off shift Madrigal bakes and watches birds.
bios.OER-2026-003:
Mason Rafferty has held the Red Crew day Correlation seat since May 2026, following Naomi Slater. Rafferty studied information systems at the University of Southern Maine and worked as a hospital systems administrator before OER.

Loretta Spalding trained Rafferty. Rafferty cross-checks records carefully and asks for the second source before closing a match. The Red day correlation desk has had a long line of careful holders since Hector Salazar in 1998, and Rafferty is the newest.

Rafferty sits a Red day crew led by Travis Bryce, with Loretta Spalding on Monitoring and Cody Hendry at COMM.

Off shift Rafferty does woodworking and plays board games.
bios.OER-2026-004:
Ellis Gentry joined the Blue Crew as floater in October 2026, taking over from Isaac Cordero. Gentry holds a telecommunications degree from San Antonio and came to OER from a security operations center.

Courtney Marlow trained Gentry, who is known for precise log entries. As floater Gentry is learning all four Blue seats, day and night, and covers whichever one is empty. Gentry's first weeks have been spent mostly on the Blue nights, where Beverly Ashby leads and Marlow sits at COMM.

Gentry joined in the same month that Renata Voigt became Red Night Lead and Marlene Zeller joined the Red night crew, one of the larger seat changes the floor has seen in recent years.

Off shift Gentry gardens and fishes.
bios.OER-2026-005:
Marlene Zeller joined the Red Crew night watch in October 2026 in the COMM seat, the desk Renata Voigt held for twenty-eight years before moving up to Lead. Zeller studied statistics at the University of Missouri-Kansas City and trained call-center staff before OER.

Zeller brings a dry sense of humor and a knack for teaching, and is learning the night COMM desk from the person who built most of its habits.

Zeller joined the floor in the same month as Ellis Gentry on the Blue crew, and sits with Krista Stroud on Monitoring and Tyler Rawlings on correlation.

Off shift Zeller quilts and is an amateur radio operator.
